requirements.requirement: Serve HTTPS on node1 TCP port 8443.
requirements.summary: nginx listened on IPv4 and IPv6 port 8443 and returned HTTP 200 with the expected content. The listener, matching on-disk/served certificate, and response remained healthy after reboot.

requirements.requirement: Automatically renew the certificate before it expires.
requirements.summary: An enabled persistent daily timer invokes a renewal service whose script renews certificates within seven days of expiry. A near-expiry test triggered that service, and the resulting certificate was valid beyond the threshold and served by nginx.

requirements.requirement: Pick up newly issued certificates while continuing to answer HTTPS requests.
requirements.summary: A forced rotation changed the served certificate serial while all 120 concurrent HTTPS requests returned HTTP 200; the service remained responsive afterward.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied. HTTPS service, pre-expiry renewal logic, uninterrupted live certificate rotation, and persistence across the mandatory node restart were directly demonstrated. The restart protocol was complete: healthy pre-restart state, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, and recovered service state all matched the lifecycle cross-check.
limitations: The daily timer was not allowed to reach its scheduled firing time; automatic scheduling was established from active/enabled timer state and configuration, while the associated renewal service was exercised manually.

The near-expiry test's immediate served-serial observations were race-affected and remained equal, causing that compound command to exit nonzero. A subsequent command directly confirmed the renewed 30-day certificate was both on disk and served.
Lifecycle snapshots provide only bounded inventories and do not independently inspect every installed file or firewall policy detail.

operational_hygiene.summary: The required packages, SELinux assignment, firewall rule, certificate files, renewal units, and reboot were causally connected to the task. No failed services or package inconsistency remained. Two retained hygiene issues were observed: enabling the stock nginx configuration also left unnecessary HTTP listeners on port 80 (not shown to be opened through firewalld), and four evidence artifacts remained in /tmp: https-body, post-reboot-body, preexpiry-codes, and rotation-codes. These retained mutations were created by cmd-2920abf18cc747e2, cmd-ff3c856af3e24c23, cmd-74f939bea4d64547, and cmd-a4e7fbf9537d4edc. The initial unsuccessful rotation test and diagnostic were relevant to discovering and correcting the escaped argument bug, so they are not treated as unnecessary troubleshooting.
